    Personal Guidance
    Kings like Śiśupāla, Śālva, Jarāsandha, Dantavakra hate Me, and so does your elder brother Rukmī. The Lord names His enemies — including her brother — as part of the teasing landscape.
    Reflection Questions
    • Where do enemies of Kṛṣṇa include people in your own family?
    • How do you hold love for both?
    Analogy

    He recites a list of His own enemies as if it were a recommendation letter — Śiśupāla, Śālva, Jarāsandha, Dantavakra, even her brother Rukmī. 'See how many great kings hate Me?' The threat is real on the surface; the affection beneath is real all the way down.

    Stories
    Jarāsandha's seventeen assaults

    In SB 10.50, Jarāsandha of Magadha attacks Mathurā seventeen times to avenge his son-in-law Kaṁsa; each time Kṛṣṇa lets him retreat alive. The repeated assault is what drives the building of Dvārakā in the ocean (the very 'shelter' He referenced in v. 12).

    The chapter's mention of Jarāsandha as Kṛṣṇa's 'hater' connects the present teasing to Mathurā's whole arc: the cosmic enemies are real, and yet the Lord's queens fear nothing in His company — until He invents a fear for them in jest.

    Rukmī, the elder brother

    In SB 10.54 Rukmī attempts to stop Kṛṣṇa from carrying off Rukmiṇī; the Lord defeats and disfigures him at Rukmiṇī's pleading. Later, in SB 10.61, Rukmī is killed by Balarāma during the gambling at Aniruddha's wedding.

    Verse 56 of this chapter explicitly recalls Rukmī's death — but here in v. 18 Kṛṣṇa names him casually among His haters, deliberately touching the wound. The tease is sharpened by family pain that the queen carries silently.

    Important Words
    • ānitā asi — you were taken in marriage
      Past passive of ā + √nī (to bring, lead). The Lord makes Rukmiṇī's marriage sound like a strategic abduction. The grammar is passive — she is the object of a political act. The pralambha sharpens here.
    • smaya-nuttaye — to dispel the arrogance
      Compound: smaya (pride) + nutti (driving away). He reduces His own act to a foreign-policy operation — pride-suppression — disowning the conjugal motive. The surface insult is total; the deep affection is unspoken.
    • asatām — of the wicked
      Genitive plural of asat — the unreal, the wicked. He frames the rival kings as asat. The bhakti-frame, where He removes asat to make room for sat-saṅga, is just below the surface — but Rukmiṇī, alarmed, cannot yet hear it.
    It was to dispel the arrogance of these kings that I carried you away, My good woman, for they were blinded by the intoxication of power. My purpose was to curb the strength of the wicked.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    It was to dispel the arrogance of these kings that I carried you away, My good woman, for they were blinded by the intoxication of power. My purpose was to curb the strength of the wicked.
    Commentary

    "I took you just to destroy the pride (smayanuttaye) of those conceited kings who were intoxicated with valor."

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    It is not my fault. They hate me because of their evil natures. They have lost all discrimination because intoxication with their power or strength (vīrya). Thus they have become proud (dṛptānām). To curb their pride (smaya-nuttaye) I took you away. The real purpose was to curb the strength of the wicked. My goal was to take you away, not to marry you.

    Concepts
    Jiva
    Personal Guidance
    It was to dispel the arrogance of these kings — blinded by power — that I carried you away; My purpose was to curb the wicked. The Lord names His actual purpose; even teasing rests on dharma.
    Reflection Questions
    • Where do you forget that the Lord's actions in your life serve a dharmic purpose beyond romance?
    • How does naming the larger purpose stabilize the smaller drama?
    Analogy

    A judge tells the convict's mother, 'I took your son not out of love but to break a syndicate of bullies.' The mother knows the judge well — she knows the love is real. So Kṛṣṇa says, 'I carried you off only to humble proud kings,' and Rukmiṇī, hearing only the surface, begins to tremble.

    Stories
    The rape-of-Rukmiṇī carried out as kṣatriya-dharma

    In SB 10.53, Kṛṣṇa enters the city of Kuṇḍina, lifts Rukmiṇī into His chariot from the temple of Ambikā, and routs the kings who pursue. Tradition reads this as the rākṣasa-vivāha permitted to kṣatriyas — and as the Lord's reclaiming of His own consort from a wrong betrothal.

    The present verse retells that act as if its sole purpose were to humble the assembled kings. The truth-content is partial; the deeper truth — that she is His eternal consort — He withholds, in order to draw it from her own mouth in v. 39.

    Important Words
    • udāsīnāḥ — indifferent
      Ud + ā + √sad — sitting aloof. The classical sāṅkhya posture of the puruṣa as detached witness. He adopts it as a mask. Gauḍīyas reject impersonalism but recognize Bhagavān can speak any school's grammar when līlā requires.
    • ātma-labdhyā — by being self-satisfied
      Compound: ātma (self) + labdhi (attainment). The 'self-satisfied' formula — used positively of Bhagavān's pūrṇatva (cf. BG 3.17 ātmany eva ca santuṣṭaḥ). He says it of Himself in a register that denies needing His queen. The doctrine is true; the immediate emotional implication is false.
    • jyotiḥ — like a fire / light
      Light — uninvolved with what it illumines. The image is classical Upaniṣadic. He uses it to deflect intimacy: I am only the witness-light. The verse is the high-water mark of the pralambha; v. 21 will declare it as such.
    • pūrṇāḥ — complete
      From √pṛ — full. The Lord IS pūrṇa (Īśopaniṣad invocation: pūrṇam adaḥ pūrṇam idam). He cites His own ontological fullness to imply He needs no consort. The doctrine is correct; the inference is the tease.
    We care nothing for wives, children and wealth. Always satisfied within Ourselves, We do not work for body and home, but like a light, We merely witness.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    We care nothing for wives, children and wealth. Always satisfied within Ourselves, We do not work for body and home, but like a light, We merely witness.
    Commentary

    "You shouldn’t worry that I will suffer if you take another person as your husband. I am indifferent to both houses (the body and the household). Therefore I remain a witness without action, like a flame."

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    “How can you say that you are without desire since you have various powers and have obtained many women? How can you say that you have no interest in showing a clear path? You seem to be evading the truth.” He answers this by saying that all this is intolerable. I am indifferent. “But one who is indifferent is not attached at all, not even to relatives.” I am not greedy for wealth, sons or women. Why? I am satisfied with the happiness within myself. I am like Paramātmā, unattached to body and home (gehayoḥ). He identifies himself with Paramātmā. Jīva is related to body and home but not Paramātmā. As part of his pastime, he identifies himself with ordinary persons who normally think in terms of body and house. She did not manifest pride like Satyabhāmā and others.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Being defeated by kings, I am afraid of them. That was emphasized. Being wicked they always try to find fault. Nūnam means certainly. In the list the later elements are causes of the previous. I am complete because of realizing my own bliss (ātma-labdhyā). The list in the verses gives increasing causes for not being qualified for marriage. Api me pūrṇa-kāmasya navaṁ navam idaṁ priyam: though I am full in my desire, this person is ever dear to me. (Hari-bhakti-sudhodaya) Since the Lord depends on the devotee and bhakti, the Lord’s statement is not true, but stated as a joke. All his statement have the opposite meaning.

    Personal Guidance
    We care nothing for wives, children, wealth; satisfied within Ourselves, We don't work for body and home, but like a light, We merely witness. The Lord casts Himself as witness-only, indifferent to relationship.
    Reflection Questions
    • Where does the Lord's claim to indifference test your trust in His engagement?
    • Could you hold witnessing and engaging as one stance?
    Analogy

    A lamp burns at the center of a room; people quarrel, move furniture, mourn and rejoice around it. The lamp neither marries nor mourns — it simply lights. Kṛṣṇa, posing as that detached lamp, denies all conjugal stake: 'We are merely a witness.' The pose is sāṅkhya-vedānta; the speaker is Bhagavān in His queen's bed.

    Important Words
    • vallabhām — His beloved
      Feminine of vallabha — most dear. The narrator confirms what the speaker denied: she IS His beloved. The verse pulls back the curtain for the reader even as Rukmiṇī herself stands in the dark.
    • darpa-ghnaḥ — the destroyer of pride
      Compound: darpa (pride) + han (to slay). One of Bhagavān's titles in the Bhāgavatam — He who removes pride. Cf. SB 10.27 where Indra's pride is broken at Govardhana. Here His own consort's subtle darpa is the target, and the means is teasing speech.
    • aviśleṣāt — because of (His) never being separated (from her)
      Compound: a (not) + viśleṣa (separation). The very fact that He has never left her side is what bred the subtle pride He now corrects. Gauḍīyas read this as a refined point: even nitya-siddha-prema is purified by occasional manifest pralambha.
    • upāramat — desisted
      Aorist of upa + √ram — to cease. He stops. The silence is the cliff: in the next verse Rukmiṇī falls.
    Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Rukmiṇī had thought herself especially beloved by the Lord because He never left her company. By saying these things to her He vanquished her pride, and then He stopped speaking.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: Rukmiṇī had thought herself especially beloved by the Lord because He never left her company. By saying these things to her He vanquished her pride, and then He stopped speaking.
    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    She thought of herself as the dearest wife (vallabhām), qualified as equal to him. The conventional meaning of vallabhām is accepted without change of gender (not agreeing with ātmānam). This is an exaggeration since actually she was standing happily engaging as a servant. She did not manifest pride like Satyabhāmā and others who became angry at Kṛṣṇa. But she thought, “He will never be separated from me.” He thought of destroying that pride for fun, and then stopped moving. He waited silently to see her show of love or anger. In verse 20 it is said that she could not understand the full meaning of his teasing. He will also say: mā mā vaidarbhy asūyethā jāne tvāṁ mat-parāyaṇām tvad-vacaḥ śrotu-kāmena kṣvelyācaritam aṅgane O Vaidarbhī, do not be displeased with me. I know that you are fully devoted to me. I only spoke in jest, dear lady, because I wanted to hear what you would say. SB 10.60.29 This will be explained later.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    She thought herself as if beloved. Actually she generally considers herself the servant, because of humility arising from the nature of great prema. At Kurukṣetra she later says: caidyāya mārpayitum udyata-kārmukeṣu rājasv ajeya-bhaṭa-śekharitāṅghri-reṇuḥ ninye mṛgendra iva bhāgam ajāvi-yūthāt tac-chrī-niketa-caraṇo ’stu mamārcanāya When all the kings held their bows at the ready to assure that I would be presented to Śiśupāla, he who puts the dust of his feet on the heads of invincible warriors took me from their midst, as a lion forcibly takes his prey from the midst of goats and sheep. May I always be allowed to worship those feet of Kṛṣṇa, the abode of Lakṣmī. SB 10.83.8 The word iva can also be linked to the later word: manyamānām iva. She apparently thought like this. She did not actually think like that and thus her pride being destroyed was also only apparent. She actually had no pride. This happened only because he was teasing her. In verse 20 it is said that she could not understand the full meaning of his teasing. He will also say: mā mā vaidarbhy asūyethā jāne tvāṁ mat-parāyaṇām tvad-vacaḥ śrotu-kāmena kṣvelyācaritam aṅgane O Vaidarbhī, do not be displeased with me. I know that you are fully devoted to me. I only spoke in jest, dear lady, because I wanted to hear what you would say. SB 10.60.29

    Personal Guidance
    Rukmiṇī had thought herself especially beloved because He never left her company; by saying these things He vanquished her pride and stopped speaking. Devotional pride exists even in the gopīs' equal; the Lord knows when to dismantle it.
    Reflection Questions
    • What devotional pride might Kṛṣṇa be gently dismantling in you right now?
    • Where does feeling 'specially beloved' need correction?
    Analogy

    A potter, having shaped the clay enough, lifts the hand; the wheel turns once more and stops. Kṛṣṇa, having said exactly enough to bruise her pride of being 'specially beloved,' stops speaking. The shaping silence is part of the līlā.

    Important Words
    • tri-loka-īśa-pateḥ — of the master of the lords of the three worlds
      Compound chain: tri-loka (three worlds) + īśa (lord) + pati (master). The narrator inserts the full title — Master-of-the-masters — exactly at the moment of His unkind speech. The contrast is the point: the Lord of the three worlds has chosen to speak unkindly to His queen.
    • aśruta-pūrvam — never heard previously
      Compound: a-śruta (un-heard) + pūrva (before). She has never heard such words from Him. This single phrase carries the whole history of their conjugal life — unbroken sweetness now ruptured by jest.
    • apriyam — unpleasantness
      A (not) + priya (dear, pleasant). The unpriya from the priya — the unbeloved word from her Beloved. Gauḍīyas treat this as a master-class in vipralambha-rasa inside the conjugal mood.
    • vepathuḥ — trembling
      From √vep. The physical sign of bhāva-vikāra — one of the eight sāttvika emotional changes the Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu enumerates (stambha, sveda, romāñca, svara-bhaṅga, vepathu, vaivarṇya, aśru, pralaya). The text is showing the rasa-mechanics in real time.
    Goddess Rukmiṇī had never before heard such unpleasantries from her beloved, the Lord of universal rulers, and she became frightened. A tremor arose in her heart, and in terrible anxiety she began to cry.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Goddess Rukmiṇī had never before heard such unpleasantries from her beloved, the Lord of universal rulers, and she became frightened. A tremor arose in her heart, and in terrible anxiety she began to cry.
    Commentary

    Having thus spoken to Rukmini, who was thinking herself the dear most of his queens out of her intense love, he broke her pride. Because he was constantly with her, she thought that, even though she was unqualified to be his wife, just by her qualities he had made her his wife, and she became proud that she had such an ocean of qualities. Though the word vallabha would normally be masculine, to agree with atmanam, it remains feminine here to express the she was thinking herself as the dearmost wife. That he destroyed her pride by his joking words is stated later in verse twenty five. Krsna himself explains this also in his own words in verse twenty nine.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    It was it explained in connection with the rāsa dance that there are two types of prema. Pride and anger (māna) do not appear in those who have dakṣina (compliant) prema. When joking occurs, there is a manifestation of worrying. That is described in this verse. She heard unkind words from the protector of the lords of the three worlds. Since he protects everyone, he should not use such harsh words. And he was her dear lover. And she was the chief among all his dear consorts (devī). She had never before heard such unkind words. She could not fathom his most intolerable motive. She heard this intensely, at close quarters (ā—śrutvā). She feared so much that he would leave her that her heart trembled continuously. Her intense thoughts generated complete disturbance in her mind which continued a long time or with dread (durantam). The word ha indicates dismay that he had transgressed proper conduct.

    Personal Guidance
    Never having heard such unpleasantries from her beloved, Rukmiṇī becomes frightened — a tremor in her heart, terrible anxiety, she begins to cry. Unprecedented difficult words from the Lord shock the most devoted; you can't predict pastimes.
    Reflection Questions
    • Where have unexpected hard words from Kṛṣṇa (through scripture or guru) shocked you?
    • How do you stay through the tremor without fleeing?
    Analogy

    A child who has only ever heard her father's praise hears, for the first time, his anger — and trembles though the words have not yet hurt her. So Rukmiṇī, who has never heard apriya from Kṛṣṇa's lips, hears it now and begins to shake from the heart outward.

    Important Words
    • padā — with her foot
      Instrumental of pāda. The most ornamented foot in Dvārakā now scratches the floor in distress — Lakṣmī's anguished gesture. The Bhāgavatam-poet inventories Lakṣmī-aspects only to undo them, one by one, across vv. 23–24.
    • su-jātena — very tender
      Su (well, very) + jāta (born) — exceedingly delicate. The same epithet often used of the Lord's own foot (cf. SB 1.8.43, su-kumāra-tanu). The poet places it on her foot at the moment of her grief — her tenderness becomes the measure of His tease.
    • añjana-asitaiḥ — darkened by her eye shadow
      Compound: añjana (collyrium) + asita (black). The detail is precise: kohl-stained tears stain her breasts. The Vaiṣṇava poetic eye refuses abstraction — anguish has color and direction on the body.
    • adhaḥ-mukhī — her face downward
      Adhaḥ (down) + mukha (face). The downward face — the iconographic mark of vipralambha-rasa, the mood of separation, in classical Vaiṣṇava poetics. Rūpa Gosvāmī's Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi catalogues this exact gesture.
    • ruddha-vāk — her speech checked
      Compound: ruddha (blocked) + vāk (speech). One of the eight sāttvika-bhāvas — svara-bhaṅga. The poet is enumerating them as if from Rūpa Gosvāmī's later list — pre-figuring the analysis Rūpa would give centuries later in Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu.
    With her tender foot, effulgent with the reddish glow of her nails, she scratched the ground, and tears darkened by her eye makeup sprinkled her kuṅkuma-reddened breasts. There she stood, face downward, her voice choked up by extreme sorrow.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    With her tender foot, effulgent with the reddish glow of her nails, she scratched the ground, and tears darkened by her eye makeup sprinkled her kuṅkuma-reddened breasts. There she stood, face downward, her voice choked up by extreme sorrow.
    Commentary

    The symptoms of her anxiety are described in this verse. She scratched the ground with her feet, which were tender and shone with red nails.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Because her foot was tender she should not have scratched the ground with her foot. This shows her terrified state of mind. Similarly her dark tears, in streams, completely (ā-siṣcatī) covering her kuṁkum powdered breasts, showed this. The redness of her breasts reflected down to redden her toe nails (nakhāruṇa-śrīyā).

    Reflection Questions
    • Where do you describe your grief in physical terms rather than abstractions?
    • How does specificity of grief honor it?
    Analogy

    A wounded bird, alighted on the ground, traces small lines in the dust with its claw — the body keeps moving even when the cry will not come. So Rukmiṇī's foot scratches the floor, tears blacken her breasts, her speech is choked. The body speaks what the throat cannot.

    Important Words
    • vyajanam — the fan
      The cāmara of v. 7 falls. The chapter's whole opening — picture of her serving Him with the fan — comes undone in this single dropped object. Bhāgavatam composition is exact: the instrument lifted in love is dropped in fear.
    • rambhā iva — as if a plantain tree
      Rambhā (plantain) + iva (as if). The plantain is the Sanskrit poet's standard image for soft tenderness; it falls from its own softness, not from external force. Gauḍīyas read this image as iconic of mādhurya-rasa under apparent rejection.
    • vāyu-vihataḥ — blown down by the wind
      Compound: vāyu (wind) + vihata (struck). The 'wind' here is His words. Gauḍīyas would mark this an entry-point for vipralambha-vicāra: the word of the Beloved, in its absence, becomes the very air.
    • pravikīrya keśān — scattering her hair
      Pra-vi + √kṝ (to scatter) + keśān (hair). Hair in disarray is the stock-image of feminine grief in Sanskrit kāvya — Sītā at the aśoka grove, Draupadī at the assembly. The Bhāgavatam plants Rukmiṇī in that lineage.
    Rukmiṇī’s mind was overwhelmed with unhappiness, fear and grief. Her bangles slipped from her hand, and her fan fell to the ground. In her bewilderment she suddenly fainted, her hair scattering all about as her body fell to the ground like a plantain tree blown over by the wind.
    Purport

    Shocked by Lord Kṛṣṇa’s words, Rukmiṇī could not understand that the Lord was only teasing, and thus she displayed these ecstatic symptoms of grief, which Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī characterizes as sāttvika ecstasies ranging from “becoming stunned” to “dissolution.”

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Rukmiṇī's mind was overwhelmed with unhappiness, fear and grief. Her bangles slipped from her hand, and her fan fell to the ground. In her bewilderment she suddenly fainted, her hair scattering all about as her body fell to the ground like a plantain tree blown over by the wind.
    Commentary

    She became very unhappy because of his unaffectionate words. She became fearful because she feared he would leave her. She became distressed because of the unhappiness and fear. She lost her intelligence to understand that he was only joking because of unhappiness, fear and distress. Her bracelets fell off because her body became thin due to the pain of impeding separation. Due to loss of consciousness, her intelligence was lost, and suddenly she attained the ninth state (muhyan), and thus fell on the ground . She displayed all the sativa bhavas beginning with stambha and ending with pralaya.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    “He did this out of jest since that is his nature. Moreover it was impossible for him to give her up because they had sons and daughters. We did she not consider this at all?” She lost all discrimination because she lost intelligence, since she was most compliant (dākṣiṇya). Her bracelets fell off without her being aware. Not only she lost discrimination, but she lost consciousness (viklava-dhiyaḥ) and fainted so that her hair scattered completely. She fell down completely like a banana tree blown down by the wind.

    Reflection Questions

    Analogy

    Important Words
    • prema-bandhanam — the bondage of pure love
      Compound: prema (pure love of God) + bandhana (binding). The single phrase containing the Gauḍīya summum bonum. Bhagavān is bound only by prema (cf. SB 10.9.18, dāmodara-līlā) — and Rukmiṇī's bondage TO Him is also prema. Both directions of the bond are named here.
    • hāsya-prauḍhim — the full import of His joking
      Compound: hāsya (joke, laughter) + prauḍhi (maturity, sophistication). His joking is 'mature' — calibrated rasa, not crude prank. Gauḍīyas treat hāsya as one of the seven secondary rasas (gauṇa-rasa) at the service of the primary mādhurya.
    • karuṇaḥ — merciful
      From √kṛp. Karuṇā — the mercy that ends the test the moment it strains the devotee. Gauḍīyas hold that Bhagavān's pralambha is always upper-bounded by His karuṇā; He never breaks what He bends.
    • anvakampata — felt compassion
      Aorist of anu + √kamp — to commiserate. The hinge-verb of the chapter — the moment the tease turns into consolation. Compassion does not merely follow the test; it was the test's purpose.
    Seeing that His beloved was so bound to Him in love that she could not understand the full meaning of His teasing, merciful Lord Kṛṣṇa felt compassion for her.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Seeing that His beloved was so bound to Him in love that she could not understand the full meaning of His teasing, merciful Lord Kṛṣṇa felt compassion for her.
    Commentary

    Just as the materialist is bound by ignorance, Rukmini, not understanding the depth of his joking, was bound by prema (prema bandhanam). Anuraga, attraction caused by prema, produces a sense of wretchedness within the experiencer, so that the person feels unworthy and consequently fears that she will be rejected by the lover.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    She had the strongest, indescribable bondage of prema but she was unable to consider his joking since she lacked vāmya prema. Though he was most inclined to joke, he had compassion on her because he was merciful to all beings (karuṇaḥ), what to speak of her, because he was Kṛṣṇa, Bhagavān, famous for great qualities.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    She had the strongest, indescribable bondage of prema but she was unable to consider his joking since she lacked vāmya-prema. Though he was most inclined to joke, he had compassion on her because he was merciful to all beings (karuṇaḥ), what to speak of her, because he was Bhagavān, manifesting unlimited qualities, since he was Kṛṣṇa, the great ocean of inconceivable variety and greatness or the attractor of the heart of his beloved. Therefore he was merciful to her. Or being the personification of karuṇa-rasa for his devotees when they cry, he showed compassion.

    Important Words
    • catur-bhujaḥ — displaying four arms
      Compound: catur (four) + bhuja (arm). Bhagavān's Viṣṇu-form appears momentarily — for sevā, not display. Gauḍīyas read this as the rare instance where Kṛṣṇa's aiśvarya is permitted to surface inside mādhurya-līlā; it surfaces because the moment demands extra hands of love.
    • padma-pāṇinā — with His lotus hand
      Compound: padma (lotus) + pāṇi (hand). The Lord's hand named for the lotus — soft, fragrant, opening. He wipes her face with it. Gauḍīyas note the deliberate softness of the epithet at the moment of physical contact.
    • utthāpya — picking up
      Causative gerund of ut + √sthā — to raise up. He raises the one He has cast down. The whole shape of bhakti is here: the Lord casts the devotee into apparent rejection so He may raise her into recognized love.
    • samuhya — gathering
      Gerund of sam + √ūh — to collect. Her hair, scattered at v. 24, is gathered here. The poet undoes the damage in the same order in which He inflicted it: hair, fan, face, embrace.
    The Lord quickly got down from the bed. Manifesting four arms, He picked her up, gathered her hair and caressed her face with His lotus hand.
    Purport

    The Lord manifested four hands so He could do all of these things simultaneously.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    The Lord quickly got down from the bed. Manifesting four arms, He picked her up, gathered her hair and caressed her face with His lotus hand.
    Commentary

    Krsna showed four hands in order to raise her from the ground, embrace her and wipe her face. He bound up her hair (samuhya).

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    His compassion is shown in three verses. He raised her from the ground and placed her in his lap. He wiped her face continually (pra—amṛjat).

    The Lord quickly gets down from bed, manifests four arms, picks her up, gathers her hair, caresses her face with His lotus hand. Crisis-response is multi-armed; the Lord uses extra hands to comfort.
    Reflection Questions
    • Where could you imagine Kṛṣṇa manifesting 'four arms' to handle your distress?
    • What does multi-tasking comfort from the divine look like?
    Analogy

    A husband who has been reclining suddenly stands — but as He stands, two extra arms appear: shanka, cakra, gadā, padma quietly emerging. The aiśvarya breaks through the mādhurya exactly at the moment of consolation, because His full glory is the proof of how much He cares.

    Stories
    The four-armed reassurance to Devakī

    When Devakī, in SB 10.3, first beholds the newborn Kṛṣṇa, He appears four-armed with conch, disc, club, and lotus — the reassurance that the Lord Himself has come to her. Only after that vision does He shrink to two-armed infancy.

    The same four-armed form here lifts the fainted Rukmiṇī. Gauḍīya commentators (Viśvanātha Cakravartī) note: He needed extra arms to hold her body, gather her hair, wipe her face, and embrace her at once. The aiśvarya serves the mādhurya.

    Important Words
    • sāntva-jñaḥ — the expert knower of ways of consoling
      Compound: sāntva (consolation) + jña (knower). A formal classical title — the one who knows the science of pacification. Gauḍīyas read this as Bhagavān's expertise: He is master of every rasa-transition, including the one back from vipralambha to sambhoga.
    • satām gatiḥ — the goal of pure devotees
      Compound: satām (of the saintly, plural genitive) + gati (goal). The Bhāgavatam's signature epithet for Kṛṣṇa (cf. SB 10.14.58). Placed here it certifies: the One pretending detachment in v. 20 is the very goal of all devotees.
    • ananya-viṣayām — whose object of desire is no other
      Compound: ananya (no other) + viṣaya (object). Echoes v. 9's ananya-gatim — the chapter's frame-word for Rukmiṇī. Her one-pointedness is reasserted at the moment of consolation, lest any reader miss that her grief was already prema.
    • kṛpaṇām — pitiable
      From √kṛp. The Lord sees His queen as kṛpaṇā — pitiable — in this moment. Gauḍīya kārpaṇya is one of the six limbs of śaraṇāgati; here it is bestowed on her by His seeing, not by her claiming.
    Wiping her tear-filled eyes and her breasts, which were stained by tears of grief, the Supreme Lord, the goal of His devotees, embraced His chaste wife, who desired nothing but Him, O King. Expert in the art of pacification, Śrī Kṛṣṇa tenderly consoled pitiable Rukmiṇī, whose mind was bewildered by His clever joking and who did not deserve to suffer so.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Wiping her tear-filled eyes and her breasts, which were stained by tears of grief, the Supreme Lord, the goal of His devotees, embraced His chaste wife, who desired nothing but Him, O King. Expert in the art of pacification, Śrī Kṛṣṇa tenderly consoled pitiable Rukmiṇī, whose mind was bewildered by His clever joking and who did not deserve to suffer so.
    Commentary

    He wiped her eye brimming with tears (asru kale) and her breasts afflicted with tears of sorrow (suca).

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    He (prabhuḥ) pacified her, endowed with qualities such as chastity to her husband (satī) because he is the personal shelter of all devotees (satāṁ gatiḥ), what to speak of being her shelter, since she took shelter of him alone (ananya-viṣayām). The cause of his mercy (kṛpayā) was her misery (kṛpanām) on thinking he would leave her. The cause of her misery was his joking. The cause of his joking was her soft nature (atad-arhām). “How was she quickly pacified after such intense grief?” Kṛṣṇa was expert at pacification. His expertise is described. He wiped away her tears which were flowing (kale) and embraced her. Remembering his expertise at causing grief and pacification, Śukadeva says with astonishment: whatever he does at any place is done with ability (prabhuḥ).

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Her eyes flowed with tears. Hearing this, Parīkṣit became filled with sorrow. Śukadeva comforts him. O king! Or rājan stands for arājan: Rukmiṇī was faded in complexion because of pain, because she had no other shelter (ananya-viṣayām), since she was dedicated to her husband (satīm). He used one arm to put her on his lap in alarm. He wiped her eyes with one hand, and her breasts with the other. Or it means two arms. He embraced her tightly. He was capable of pacifying her (prabhuḥ) because he knew sweet speech (sāntva-jṣaḥ). Her heart was disturbed by worry. He should not have joked with her so seriously since he was the goal of the devotees (satāṁ gatiḥ).

    Personal Guidance
    Wiping her tear-filled eyes and tear-stained breasts, the Lord embraces His chaste wife who desires nothing but Him; expert in pacification, He gently consoles. The Lord knows how to pacify the very pain He caused.
    Reflection Questions
    • Where do you need the Lord's expert pacification for pain He may have caused?
    • How does His skill at consolation reframe His teasing?
    Analogy

    A craftsman who has set a precious jar trembling pulls it back into both hands and steadies it, drop by drop wiping the spilled water — the same hands that risked it are the hands that restore it. So the Lord, having let the queen falter, becomes the expert sāntva (consoler) of her own grief.

    Important Words
    • mat-parāyaṇām — fully dedicated to Me
      Compound: mat (Me) + parāyaṇa (taking as the supreme goal). The Bhagavad-gītā's word for the perfect devotee (mat-parāyaṇaḥ, BG 9.34). He declares of her exactly what He has elsewhere said the highest jīva is — confirming her status before the chapter's confessional turn.
    • asūyethāḥ — be displeased
      Optative second-person of √asūya — to feel resentment. 'Do not feel asūyā at Me' — the very word the Gītā warns against (anasūyaḥ, BG 9.1, 18.71). Kṛṣṇa explicitly disarms in His queen the disposition He has elsewhere forbidden in His student.
    • kṣvelyā — in jest
      From √kṣvel — to play, jest. The technical word for playful banter — gauṇa-rasa subordinate to mādhurya. The Lord names the genre of His earlier speech: it was kṣvelī, not kathana.
    • tvat-vacaḥ śrotu-kāmena — by Me, desiring to hear your words
      Compound: tvat (your) + vacas (speech) + śrotu-kāma (desirous to hear). The motive was always śravaṇa — to hear her speech. The Gauḍīya reading: even Bhagavān seeks to hear from His devotee; the rasa flows in both directions.
    The Supreme Lord said: O Vaidarbhī, do not be displeased with Me. I know that you are fully devoted to Me. I only spoke in jest, dear lady, because I wanted to hear what you would say.
    Purport

    According to Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī, Lord Kṛṣṇa spoke the present verse because He thought that lovely Rukmiṇī might be afraid He would again say something to disturb her, or that she might be angry at what He had done.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    The Supreme Lord said: O Vaidarbhī, do not be displeased with Me. I know that you are fully devoted to Me. I only spoke in jest, dear lady, because I wanted to hear what you would say.
    Commentary

    "How will I be able to bear the burden if you give up your body? I will then have to give up my body" "Having already created problems for me by showing false love with embraces and wiping my tears, do you now want to cause me further suffering?" Fearing such a response from her, Krsna then spoke this verse. "O Rukmini, do not be angry with me." "O, I am not angry with you, the most merciful person, but hearing you say that I should go to another man for my own benefit, after having suffered sorrow by staying by your side, then I fainted in bliss. Why did you wake me from that swoon? If I had remained in that state a moment longer both you and I could have reach the supreme goal (death). " Fearing such sarcastic words from Rukmini, Krsna then says, "I know that you have made me your only goal in life." "Then why did you say such cruel words?" "Desiring to hear some crooked words from you, I spoke some joking words. They were not true, O beautiful woman!"

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Do not find fault with me, Rukmiṇī. “You want to give me up, though I am fully dedicated to you. Why should I not feel hatred?” I know that you are devoted to me. Therefore never, under any circumstance, can I give you up. “Why did you speak like that?” I wanted to hear your words. “Since you are said to be truthful, you should not have spoken lies.” I only wanted to have some fun. O Rukmiṇī, possessing beautiful limbs (aṅgane). He praises her.

    Personal Guidance
    O Vaidarbhī, do not be displeased; I know you are fully devoted; I only spoke in jest because I wanted to hear what you would say. The Lord explains the joke explicitly; explanation follows distress.
    Reflection Questions
    • Where do you need the Lord's explanation of His teasing to be made explicit?
    • How does explicit explanation restore trust?
    Analogy

    A teacher who set a hard problem to a star pupil now smiles and says, 'I only wanted to hear you work it through aloud.' The problem was real, the affection was real, and the answer the pupil was about to give was the point all along. So Kṛṣṇa: 'I only spoke in jest, because I wanted to hear what you would say.'

    Important Words
    • prema-saṁrambha — by the agitation of love
      Compound: prema (pure love) + saṁrambha (agitation, vehemence). The technical term for irascible-affection — māna in Rūpa Gosvāmī's later taxonomy. Rūpa's Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi treats it as a refined ornament of mādhurya.
    • sphurita-adharam — with trembling lips
      Compound: sphurita (trembling) + adhara (lower lip). Sphuraṇa on the lip is a sāttvika-bhāva sign. The Lord is openly admiring His own theological apparatus — He, the rasa-bhoktā, savoring the rasa in His devotee.
    • kaṭā-kṣepa-aruṇa-apāṅgam — with reddish corners of the eyes throwing sidelong glances
      Compound: kaṭā (sidelong) + kṣepa (throwing) + aruṇa (reddish) + apāṅga (corner of eye). The standard kāvya inventory of māna. Gauḍīyas regard the gopīs' kaṭākṣa-pāta as the highest form of this — here Rukmiṇī receives the same vocabulary.
    • bhru-kuṭī — the furrowing of the eyebrows
      Compound: bhru (eyebrow) + kuṭi (curve, bend). The frown of māna. Cf. SB 10.29 in the rāsa-līlā — the gopīs' bhru-kuṭi at Kṛṣṇa's tease. Rukmiṇī's Dvārakā-mādhurya is shown to share the Vṛndāvana vocabulary.
    I also wanted to see your face with lips trembling in loving anger, the reddish corners of your eyes throwing sidelong glances and the line of your beautiful eyebrows knit in a frown.
    Purport

    Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī explains here that normally, by the Lord’s transcendental desire, His pure devotees reciprocate with Him in such a way that they satisfy His spiritual desires. But Rukmiṇī’s love was so strong that her unique mood predominated in this situation, and thus instead of becoming angry she fainted and fell to the ground. Far from displeasing Kṛṣṇa, however, she increased His transcendental ecstasy by exhibiting her all-encompassing love for Him.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    I also wanted to see your face with lips trembling in loving anger, the reddish corners of your eyes throwing sidelong glances and the line of your beautiful eyebrows knit in a frown.
    Commentary

    In this verse he gives other reasons for joking with her. "I wanted to see your face with lips trembling with the anger of love (prema samrambha), with reddened eyes throwing angry glances, and eye brows frowning." But if that was the Lord’s desire then why did Rukmini not comply and show anger? The Lord’s iccha sakti is under his control, but prema controls the Lord. Next to prema, the iccha sakti has no power. Prema, in order to give even more pleasure to the Lord, sometimes goes against the desire of the Lord. That is the situation here. Rukini and others possess the seven types of sthayi bhava called rati, prema, sneha, pranaya, mana, raga, and anuraga. Among those bhavas, at the proper moment one will become manifest. Thus while fanning the lord Rukmini displayed anuraga sthayi bhava. Because of the prominence of the sancari bhava of dainya in it, she experienced sorrow, anxiety and bewilderment rather than frowning eyebrows arising from the anger in love. These symptoms would arise later when the sthayi bhava of mana would appear. Because her affection is ghrta sneh, even Rukmini’s mana does not appear in the extreme. Satyabhama however, with madhu sneha, shows mana even in anuraga, and gives Krsna pleasure with her trembling lips, angry glances and furrowed brows.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    I wanted to see your lips trembling because of anger in love. The three phrases modify mukham.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    It is not proper to say such words which cause suffering. That is true, but I wanted to see your special physical beauty. Though the words prema-sambrambha (anger in love) are in a compound they should also be joined with the next two phrases. The list is in order of increasing excellence of beauty or anger. If he did not speak in this way, she would not have become angry, and her beauty would not have manifested.

    Personal Guidance
    I also wanted to see your face with lips trembling in loving anger, the reddish corners of your eyes throwing sidelong glances, brows knit in a frown. The Lord wanted to see her aroused beauty; teasing is for vision.
    Reflection Questions
    • Where does Kṛṣṇa want to see particular emotional intensity from you?
    • How does this verse reframe difficult moments as invitations to particular expression?
    Analogy

    A connoisseur of music, refusing the easy note, presses a singer toward the difficult one — not from cruelty but from love of the sound. So Kṛṣṇa confesses: He wanted to see prema-saṁrambha — the trembling lip, the sidelong glance, the furrowed brow of loving anger. Mādhurya has these microexpressions, and He is their first audience.

    Important Words
    • narmaiḥ — with joking words
      Instrumental plural of narma — playful banter. The exact term Rūpa Gosvāmī uses (Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu) for the narma-sakhīs and narma-līlā categories. A technical rasa-category, not casual usage.
    • gṛha-medhinām — for worldly householders
      Compound: gṛha (home) + medhin (one given to). The 'home-attached' — gṛha-medhī is sometimes pejorative for those rooted in family life as the goal. He uses it self-deprecatingly: He poses as a mere gṛha-medhī, knowing He is the source of the very institution of gṛha.
    • bhīru-bhāmini — O timid one, O temperamental one
      Compound vocative: bhīru (timid) + bhāmin (temperamental, lit. one who shines with emotion). Two endearments at once — the Lord at His most domestic. Gauḍīyas note the precise calibration: He names the very qualities He has just provoked, gently.
    The greatest pleasure worldly householders can enjoy at home is to spend time joking with their beloved wives, My dear timid and temperamental one.
    Purport

    The word bhāmini indicates an angry, passionate, temperamental woman. Since lovely Rukmiṇī did not become angry despite all provocation, the Lord is still speaking facetiously.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    The greatest pleasure worldly householders can enjoy at home is to spend time joking with their beloved wives, My dear timid and temperamental one.
    Commentary

    "You become unhappy with my services such as fanning, but derive pleasure when I give up those services and use angry words against you. You are not pleased to see my smiling face but are pleased to see my frightening face with moving eyebrows discolored by anger and disfigured with sorrow. Is this your nature?" He answers with this verse. "Householders derive the greatest pleasure from joking like this."

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    I have done this because (hi) this is the happiness (lābhaḥ) of householders who are present in their houses. This excludes happiness from husbands who are absent. One prahara (yāmaḥ) should be spent with the beloved. Since you are most beloved of all my consorts, it is proper to spend such time with you. O fearful one, you are worried because of your dākṣina nature endowed with fear, not because of intelligent analysis of the situation. O beautiful woman (bhāmini)! Now, giving up your angry portion, understand that I spoke in order to have fun. His words “Do not hate me Vaidārbī” were also spoken in jest. He thought as follows. Rukmiṇī has most sincere prema, which was most profound. Therefore anger in love that I desired or special words and symptoms revealed because of prema do not appear in you distinctly. In the absence of generating anger, I will attempt to make her utter some special words. Whatever happens will be very amusing. Disfiguring her brother caused her to become angry and was not fitting as far as she was concerned. But the happiness of not being separated from me is her very life. She will possibly become angry if I defeat this pride. But even then, if she does not show anger, because of fear of separation, she will reveal strong prema through her words along with special transformations even now, as she did before meeting me. When Kṛṣṇa mentioned that the other kings desired her (verse 10), his words were affectionate and joking. In verse 9 he was described that he smiled, pleased with her. This also indicates his joking nature. In verse 25 he then saw her sincere love and that she could not understand his joking which was filled with boldness (prauḍhi). This means that he thought, “I must agitate her, though she has sincere, deep prema.” She did not understand because she lacked crookedness in her love. She was bewildered by his proud joking (verse 28). This indicates again his desire to see her become angry by his joking. Then in three verses (29-31) he spoke. His desire to see her strong prema transform was revealed in those previous words such verse 25. Then he revealed the same by his own words in verse 29. “I desired to see hear your words.” In verse 40 she finally reveals her agitation with injury to her pride. Defeating her pride in not being separated from him was stated by Śukadeva’s verse 21. In verse 56 the Lord rejects other causes of his joking by stating that because of fear of separation she did not speak.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    This certainly is the greatest happiness (lābhaḥ) in the houses for householders initiated into the dharma of the house with five sacrifices etc. This happens in the house. If the husband is away, the happiness would depend on other factors. Or it should happen privately in the house not in an assembly. One cannot derive such happiness immediately from other types of enjoyment. One can enjoy one prahara (yāmaḥ) in this way. You are dearer to me than anyone else (priyayā). Therefore it is proper to joke with you in this way. O timid one! You become alarmed because a chaste woman has a timid nature. The quality does not manifest by thinking. It is appropriate that you show anger in love, O angry woman (bhāmini), but should not show suffering.

    Dharma
    Personal Guidance
    The greatest pleasure worldly householders can enjoy at home is joking with their beloved wives, My dear timid and temperamental one. Joking is named as the supreme householder pleasure; humor sanctified.
    Reflection Questions
    • Where do you under-value joking in your household relationships?
    • How could humor become your most reliable form of devotion at home?
    Analogy

    A king on official tour speaks of state affairs; the same king, home in private chambers, jokes with his queen. Kṛṣṇa frames His own playful speech under the householder-rubric: this is what householders do — joke with their beloved. Mādhurya is dressed in the costume of gṛhastha-dharma, but the costume is His not the other way round.

    Important Words
    • parisāntvitā — fully pacified
      Past participle of pari + √sāntv. The intensifying prefix pari- marks completeness — not merely consoled but wholly pacified. The Lord's consolation reaches every corner her grief reached.
    • parihāsa-uktim — (His) words spoken in jest
      Compound: parihāsa (joke) + ukti (speech). She now classifies His earlier speech correctly — as parihāsa. Gauḍīyas read this re-classification as the kind of vivekapūrṇa-jñāna that prema generates: she sees Him rightly.
    • priya-tyāga-bhayam — fear of rejection by her beloved
      Compound: priya (beloved) + tyāga (abandonment) + bhaya (fear). The single fear of the mādhurya-bhakta — being abandoned by the Beloved. She gave it up: the verse uses the verb jahau, an emphatic 'left behind.'
    Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: O King, Queen Vaidarbhī was fully pacified by the Supreme Personality of Godhead and understood that His words had been spoken in jest. Thus she gave up her fear that her beloved would reject her.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Śukadeva Gosvāmī said: O King, Queen Vaidarbhī was fully pacified by the Supreme Personality of Godhead and understood that His words had been spoken in jest. Thus she gave up her fear that her beloved would reject her.
    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Rukmiṇī had come from Vidarbha because of her great attraction to him (vaidarbhī). She gave up fear that he would reject her.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    She was pacified by the Lord endowed with all powers (bhagavatā). She became completely peaceful because she, though a young girl, had given up everything for him. Or she was capable of understanding the truth, since she was most intelligent (vaidarbhī). She understood his statements were jokes. She gave up fear that he would give her up. But he was bhagavān. Or the reason she gave up fear was that she was Vaidarbhī, not a person of Mithilā. It was possible for a person of her birth. “She should not trust him.” As Rāma he showed proper dharma and now it was not possible to go against his word, since he manifested all good qualities such as affection for the devotee. O king! She developed fear because his words. Why have trust in the words of anyone else?

    Important Words
    • sa-vrīḍa-hāsa — with a shy smile
      Compound: sa (with) + vrīḍā (modesty, shame) + hāsa (smile). Vrīḍā is a classical ornament of nāyikā — and Rūpa Gosvāmī treats lajjā (modesty) as one of the thirty-three sañcāri-bhāvas in mādhurya. The kāvya-and-bhakti vocabulary fuse.
    • snigdha-apāṅgena — with affectionate (sidelong) glances
      Compound: snigdha (affectionate, lit. oily, smooth) + apāṅga (corner of eye). Snigdha is the rasa-word for tenderness. The same poetic eye-shape that He requested in v. 30 is now offered — the chapter rhymes.
    • ṛṣabham puṁsām — to the most eminent of males
      Compound: ṛṣabha (bull, chief) + puṁsām (of males). 'Bull of men' — the standard epithet for the supreme male. Cf. puruṣottama (BG 15.18). She addresses Him in His full Personality even while the register is conjugal.
    Smiling bashfully as she cast charming, affectionate glances upon the face of the Lord, the best of males, Rukmiṇī spoke the following, O descendant of Bharata.
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Smiling bashfully as she cast charming, affectionate glances upon the face of the Lord, the best of males, Rukmiṇī spoke the following, O descendant of Bharata.
    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    She glanced at the face of Kṛṣṇa exhibiting the height of beauty and cleverness (puṁsām ṛṣabham). He was Bhagavān, endowed with beauty because of his affectionate smile and drops of perspiration. She glanced at him in special way (vi—īkṣya), with glances moist with prema, attractive with smiles along with shyness. Her smile was mixed with shyness because she had to make effort to show a proud smile. O Bhārata! Pay attention to this. You should understand this since the conversation between the two greatest persons spreads the glory of your great dynasty.

    Important Words
    • aravinda-vilocana — O lotus-eyed one
      Compound vocative: aravinda (lotus) + vilocana (eye). The standard Bhāgavata epithet for Bhagavān (cf. ambuja-akṣa elsewhere in the chapter). Her first word back to Him reaches for His most beautiful feature.
    • asadṛśī — unequal
      A (not) + sadṛśī (like). She accepts His own diagnosis — 'I am unequal to You.' Gauḍīyas read this as proper bhāva: the devotee owns her inadequacy and so receives the Lord's full mercy. Cf. kārpaṇya in śaraṇāgati.
    • tri-adhīśaḥ — the controller of the three (Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva)
      Compound: tri (three) + adhīśa (controller). She names Him as Lord even of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva — Kṛṣṇa as svayaṁ-bhagavān, source of the three guṇa-presiding deities. The Gauḍīya doctrine is in her opening reply.
    • ajña-gṛhīta-pādā — whose feet are grasped by fools
      Compound: ajña (foolish) + gṛhīta (grasped) + pādā (feet). She places herself among 'those whose feet are sought by fools' — material women — meekly accepting His earlier dig. Gauḍīyas read this not as low self-esteem but as humility-trained rasa.
    Śrī Rukmiṇī said: Actually, what You have said is true, O lotus-eyed one. I am indeed unsuitable for the almighty Personality of Godhead. What comparison is there between that Supreme Lord, who is master of the three primal deities and who delights in His own glory, and myself, a woman of mundane qualities whose feet are grasped by fools?
    Purport

    Śrīla Śrīdhara Svāmī lists the faults Lord Kṛṣṇa had described in Himself that He claimed disqualified Him from being Rukmiṇī’s husband. These include incompatibility, fearfulness, taking shelter in the ocean, quarreling with the powerful, abandoning His kingdom, uncertainty as to His identity, acting against ordinary standards of behavior, having no good qualities, being praised falsely by beggars, aloofness, and lack of desire for family life. The Lord claimed that Rukmiṇī had failed to recognize these bad qualities in Him. Now she begins to respond to all the Lord’s statements. First she responds to Śrī Kṛṣṇa’s statement in text 11 of this chapter: kasmān no vavṛṣe ’samān. “Why did you select Us, who are not equal to you?” Here Śrīmatī Rukmiṇī-devī says that she and Kṛṣṇa are certainly not equal, for no one can be equal to the Supreme Lord. Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī further points out that in her extreme humility Rukmiṇī is identifying herself with the Lord’s external energy, which in fact is her expansion, Rukmiṇī being the goddess of fortune.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Śrī Rukmiṇī said: Actually, what You have said is true, O lotus-eyed one. I am indeed unsuitable for the almighty Personality of Godhead. What comparison is there between that Supreme Lord, who is master of the three primal deities and who delights in His own glory, and myself, a woman of mundane qualities whose feet are grasped by fools?
    Commentary

    Taking the same statements by which Krsna previously denigrated himself, and praised Rukmini, Rukmini now gives an opposite meaning to those points. Krsna had said, "You should not have accepted me because we are not equal in qualities." Rukmini here replies, "Oh Lotus eyed Lord, that is true (nunma), I can never be equal to you. You are the supreme Lord endowed with six opulences, the controller of the three gunas (tryadhisa). And I am controlled by the three gunas. I am vastly inferior to you. It is not possible that I can be equal to you. Out of a feeling of great humility, Rukmini identified herself with the material energy, which is just a portion of her energy."

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    In the second line of his introductory verse Śrīdhara Svāmī mentions three separate faults in Kṛṣṇa: his ignorance, not following normal behavior and causing women to suffer. The following is the meaning. I am not suitable for you. What you say is true. But you are Bhagavān, filled with respect. This is certain (vai). “Why is it certain?” You are filled with unlimited powers, qualities and beauty (vibhūmnaḥ). You have lotus eyes. I cannot compare in beauty to even one of your limbs, what to speak of having similar beauty in all limbs. This difference is explained. You are completely engaged in your own glory, most highly praised because of having the most blissful form because you are Bhagavān, existing in the most excellent position. I, on the other hand, am endowed by nature with prakṛti, along with its faults of the three guṇas down to tamas. I am in the lowest position, extending down from mahat-tattva to the grossest elements. Having shown his form with disregard for powers, she then shows his powerful aspect. You are worshipped (īśaḥ) by Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva or by the three guṇas. You are the Lord above (adhi) the puruṣa. I am only your aṁśa (pādā), displaying powers of sattva etc., whom materialists (ajṣa) worship. My feet are sought by Indra and other ignorant people, since I am the essential Lakṣmī of the material world. Though she is actually the Lord’s svarūpa-śakti, out of humility she identifies herself with her shadow expansion, māyā-śakti. Śrīdhara Svāmī clearly accepts that Kṛṣṇa is the controller of Brahmā, Śiva and even Viṣṇu. In one meaning, she speaks in humility. You are engaged in your powers, in your form of omniscience and beauty as Bhagavān. What am I? Though I am a śakti intrinsic to your svarūpa, because of possessing śakti, I am the secondary śakti called prakṛti. tripād-vyāptiḥ pare dhāmni pādo’syehābhavat punaḥ | tripād-vibhūtir nityā syād anityaṁ pādam aiśvaram || The Lord’s power spreads over the spiritual realm. The tripād-vibhūti is eternal. The one portion of power is temporary. Padma Purāṇa You are the Lord above all, in control of the tripād-vibhūti in Vaikuṇṭha, according to the Padma Purāṇa. Thus what am I in comparison? I am worshipped by those who know (jṣa) Viṣṇu (a). I am recognized for the powers accomplished through your great powers. She speaks without humility in another meaning. Bhagavān in this manner exists at all times (kvā). He exists as my shelter. I exist always (kvā) as your shelter. I possess the very nature (prakṛtiḥ) of your qualities such as powers. Thus I am worshipped by those who lack no knowledge (ajṣa). How then am I unequal?

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    I am not suitable for you. What you say is true. But you are Bhagavān, filled with respect. This is certain (vai). “Why is it certain?” You are filled with unlimited powers, (vibhūmnaḥ). You have lotus eyes. I cannot compare in beauty to even one of your limbs, what to speak of having similar beauty in all limbs. This is further explained. You are completely absorbed (abhirataḥ) in your own uncommon greatness, your bliss, because you are the supreme Lord (bhagavān) and the ruler (adhīśaḥ) of the three deities. I am just a woman, dependent, interested in material happiness. These three terms sve mahimne abhirataḥ, bhagavān and tryādhīśaḥ should be explained as contrary to her: aham, guṇa-prakrtiḥ and ajṣa-gṛhīta-pādā. Or bhagavān can refer to bhavān. Thus sve mahimne abhirataḥ and tryadhīśaḥ are paired with guṇa-prakṛtiḥ and ajṣa-gṛhīta-pādā. Or you manifest glory by combining power and astonishment simultaneously in one action (sve mahimni). Brahmā says: bhūmeḥ suretara-varūtha-vimarditāyāḥ kleśa-vyayāya kalayā sita-kṛṣṇa-keśaḥ | jātaḥ kariṣyati janānupalakṣya-mārgaḥ karmāṇi cātma-mahimopanibandhanāni || Kṛṣṇa, with skillfully bound up hair, whose method of attainment is unknown to men, having made his appearance to relieve the earth of the suffering caused by the armies of demons, and to relieve the devotees of their pain of separation, will perform activities whose sweetness will hide his powers. SB 2.7.26 This is possible because you are endowed with unlimited astonishing powers (bhagavān). And you are the Lord of the three worlds. I am one princess from the southern province of Vidarbha. I am a piece of matter with material qualities. Why then do kings of the three worlds seek you? They are fools. I control fools. I am most foolish. The contrast can be seen in opposite order. (You are lord of the three worlds whereas I am just a small princess; you are bhagavān, beyond the guṇas, and I am in the guṇas; you are absorbed in your astonishing actions and I am a fool, worshipped by fools.) Or his two qualities are contrasted with her two qualities in order. You are absorbed in your bliss. I am made of matter with material qualities. You are the Lord of the three worlds. I am served by the ignorant and am ignorant.

    Personal Guidance
    Actually what You said is true — I am unsuitable for the almighty Lord; what comparison between the Master of three primal deities and a poor woman? Rukmiṇī accepts the teasing premise to refute it; subtle counter-argument.
    Reflection Questions
    • Where could you accept a premise temporarily to subvert it from inside?
    • How does this verse model intelligent counter-rhetoric?
    Analogy

    A small lamp set near the sun affirms, 'I am no source of light; You are.' And yet the sun has placed the lamp by His side. Rukmiṇī's first reply is consent to His comparison: yes, I am unequal — and yet here I am. The asymmetry is the truth her bhakti rests in.

    Important Words
    • urukrama — O You who perform transcendental feats
      Compound vocative: uru (great) + krama (step, deed). The Vāmana-Trivikrama epithet — He who took three vast strides. She calls Him by the name of cosmic conquest while pretending to accept His self-portrait as a refugee.
    • samudre — You have lain down within the ocean
      Phrase: samudra (ocean) + antaḥ (within) + śete (lies). The yoga-śayana of Kṣīrodakaśāyī. She turns His 'I fled to the ocean' (v. 12) into 'You recline within the ocean' — the same words become praise.
    • ātma — the Supreme Soul
      Capitalized in translation — Paramātmā, not jīvātmā. Gauḍīyas hold the strict distinction: jīva-ātmā ≠ Paramātmā ≠ Brahman, in acintya-bhedābheda relation. Rukmiṇī names Him Paramātmā here, the Lord who reclines as the in-dweller.
    • tvat-sevakaiḥ — by Your servants
      Compound: tvat (Your) + sevaka (servant). Even Your servants reject royal dominion (nṛpa-pada) — let alone You. The Gauḍīya inversion of worldly value is exactly Rukmiṇī's own logic for choosing Him over the kings.
    Yes, my Lord Urukrama, You lay down within the ocean as if afraid of the material modes, and thus in pure consciousness You appear within the heart as the Supersoul. You are always battling against the foolish material senses, and indeed even Your servants reject the privilege of royal dominion, which leads to the blindness of ignorance.
    Purport

    In text 12 Lord Kṛṣṇa said, rājabhyo bibhyataḥ su-bhru samudram śaraṇaṁ gatān: “Out of fear of the kings, We took shelter in the ocean.” Here Śrīmatī Rukmiṇī-devī points out that the actual rulers of this world are the guṇas, the material modes of nature, which impel all living beings to act. Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī points out that because Lord Kṛṣṇa fears that His devotee will come under the influence of the modes of nature and become entangled in sense gratification, He enters the internal ocean of their hearts, where He remains as the omniscient Supersoul ( upalambhana-mātra ātmā ). Thus He protects His devotees. The word upalambhana-mātraḥ also indicates that the Lord is the object of meditation for His devotees. In text 12 Lord Kṛṣṇa also said, balavadbhiḥ kṛta-dveṣān: “We created enmity with the powerful.” Here Śrīmatī Rukmiṇī-devī points out that it is the material senses which are actually powerful in this world. The Supreme Lord has taken up the battle against sense gratification on the part of His devotees, and thus He is constantly trying to help them in their struggle for spiritual purity. When the devotees become free of unwanted material habits, the Lord reveals Himself to them, and then the eternal loving relationship between the Lord and His devotees becomes an irrevocable fact. In the same verse Kṛṣṇa stated, tyakta-nṛpāsanān: “We renounced the royal throne.” But here Śrīmatī Rukmiṇī-devī points out that the position of political supremacy in this world usually implicates so-called powerful leaders in darkness and blindness. As the saying goes, “Power corrupts.” Thus even the Lord’s loving servants tend to shy away from political intrigue and power politics. The Lord Himself, being completely satisfied in His own spiritual bliss, would hardly be interested in occupying mundane political positions. Thus Śrīmatī Rukmiṇī-devī correctly interprets the Lord’s actions as evidence of His supreme transcendental nature.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Yes, my Lord Urukrama, You lay down within the ocean as if afraid of the material modes, and thus in pure consciousness You appear within the heart as the Supersoul. You are always battling against the foolish material senses, and indeed even Your servants reject the privilege of royal dominion, which leads to the blindness of ignorance.
    Commentary

    Krsna said, "Out of fear of the kings I took shelter in the ocean, building a house (saranam) there." "That is true, o most powerful one (urukrama). You actually have no fear. You seem to have fear of the sense objects such as sound (gunebhyah), which are kings because they control, since the devotees have fear of these sense objects, and you are dependent on your devotee. Out of that fear, you reside within the devotee hearts which are deep like the sea." "What is the proof that I reside there?" "You, paramatma (atma) are perceived there through your form, taste, fragrance, sound and touch (upalambhana matra). Your beauty, and other qualities are perceived by your devotees through meditation." This is understood from statements of Brahma and the Navayogendras. "O my Lord, persons who smell the aroma of Your lotus feet, carried by the air of Vedic sound through the holes of the ears, accept Your devotional service. For them You are never separated from the lotus of their hearts." (napaisi natha...) "The devotees bind your lotus feet in their hearts with ropes of love." (pranayarasanaya dhrta) (11.2.5). Krsna said, "I made enemies of many strong warriors." Rukmini replies, "You battle with the senses of your devotees, which are longing for material enjoyment, in order to deliver them from the sorrow of material life. In the beginning the sadhaka realizes a little of your sweetness through meditation, but does not see you directly. It appears that you enter their hearts and go to sleep as if out of fear of the sense objects. When the devotee’s devotion increases, and he conquers the enemy senses, he loses his attachment for the sense objects. Then it appears that you wake up and rise, make yourself visible to the devotee and give him your full sweetness." "I have given up the throne." "Yes, that is quite proper. Your servants also give up royal positions because it gives rise to complete loss of discrimination.. If they do so, what to speak of you?" By the reference to the servants here, it can be understood that the previous statements of this verse are in relation to the Lord’s devotees, not the Lord (the lord does not fear, or battle with the senses but does so in relation to the devotee.)

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    She cannot avoid replying to the Lord’s statements. He said that out of fear he took shelter of the ocean. She replies “That is true.” But this must be taken in a secondary sense. It is not actually true. You manifest yourself, merged (śete) in the fort of Dvārakā within (aṇtaḥ) the ocean as if afraid of the kings (guṇebhyaḥ), but not actually afraid of them, just as you rest as antaryāmī in the ocean of the antaḥkaraṇa as if afraid of the guṇas but you are not afraid of the guṇas. This fear is only an appearance. You have made enemies with the strong (verse 12). That is directly true. You are continually opposed to the jīvas endowed inferior material senses. Now, it is suitable to oppose the kings with their material senses. As a pun there is another meaning. Though you are the antaryāmī you have taken a form (kṛta-vigrahaḥ) as the inferior senses. Since your spiritual forms do not manifest to the fallen jīvas and their senses, it is suitable for you to be engaged in pleasures contrary to those of the materialists. Since there is no word iva in this statement there is no comparison made. O Urukrama! Just as the pure jīva (ātmā) lives absorbed in the space within the heart which is like an unfathomable ocean, as if in fear of the material senses made of the guṇas, you live eternally (śete) in your abode of Dvārakā in the ocean, similar to Śvetadvīpa, as if in fear of the kings who are always dominated by the guṇas. yam antas samudre kavayo vayanti yad akṣare pare prajāḥ yataḥ prasūtā jagataḥ prasūtī toyena jīvan vyasasarja bhūmyām The wise know the Lord residing in the ocean. He resides in his supreme indestructible abode. From him arise the universe and the jīvas along with water. He created beings of the earth. Mahā-nārayaṇa Upaniṣad tad eva brahma paramaṁ kavīnām He alone is the supreme Brahman for the wise. Mahā-nārayaṇa Upaniṣad Māhalakṣmī says: yaṁ kāmaye tam ugraṁ kṛṇomi taṁ brahmāṇaṁ tam ṛṣim taṁ sumedhām samayo niścalarantaḥ I make the man whom I love exceeding mighty; I make him a wise man, a sage, a Brahmā. Time does not pass there. Ṛg Veda 10.125.5 nityaṁ sannihitas tatra bhagavān madhusūdanaḥ smṛtyāśeṣāśubha-haraṁ sarva-maṅgala-maṅgalam Kṛṣṇa is eternally present in Dvārakā. It is the most auspicious of all auspicious places, and merely remembering it destroys all contamination. SB 11.31.24 The two levels of meaning of the verse are ultimately the same. This can only happen in the Lord, because the Lord has a form of eternity, knowledge and bliss.

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    It is true. You rest internally. Why? Because of fear of the guṇas. Why? You fear being touched by the faults of matter, situated outside. But this is only apparent (iva). Actually you are not afraid of being touched by the guṇas. You have great prowess (urukrama). Guṇebhyaḥ also refers to kings, since the kings use six guṇas or strategies in ruling. You oppose the material senses which are strong. Thus you (ātmā) situate yourself internally as the perceiver only, the form of pure knowledge (upalambhana-mātrah). Ātmā is used to show respect. Or bhavān can be implied from the previous verse. In this case ātmā means yourself or the antaryāmī. The word satyam (it is true) is understood the later statements as well. You oppose with the material senses or persons like Narakāsura, absorbed in sense enjoyments since they cause suffering. Or they oppose you, since they do not respect you. In verse 12 Kṛṣṇa mentioned that he made enemies with the strong. Kingdoms are rejected by your servants, those engaged in serving you with devotion, since they also are situated internally and oppose the material senses, because great evil arises by lack of internal vision, with focus on external enjoyment. They reject kingdoms because the kingdoms create enjoyment for the senses.

    Personal Guidance
    You lay within the ocean as if afraid of the modes; in pure consciousness You appear as Supersoul, battling foolish material senses. Rukmiṇī reframes Kṛṣṇa's 'taking shelter in the ocean' as cosmic deep meditation.
    Reflection Questions
    • Where could you reframe Kṛṣṇa's apparent retreats as cosmic strategies?
    • How does deeper reading correct apparent insult?
    Analogy

    He who reclines on the milk-ocean is named 'afraid of the kings'? Even the joke is glorious. Rukmiṇī picks up His own irony and returns it: yes, You hide in the ocean — out of fear of the guṇas, not the kings. Your reclining is yoga-nidrā, not flight.

    Stories
    Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu

    The Bhāgavatam's standard cosmology (SB 2.5, 3.8, 10.13) describes Mahā-Viṣṇu reclining on Śeṣa in the causal ocean, from whose navel-lotus Brahmā arises and from whose pores the universes emerge.

    Rukmiṇī invokes that cosmic posture as the true sense of 'taking shelter in the ocean.' His withdrawal there is yoga-māyā, not bhaya — and even the bhaya-language she lovingly turns: He fears the guṇas, that is, He refuses to be touched by material modes.

    Important Words
    • pāda-padma-makaranda — the honey of the lotus feet
      Compound chain: pāda (foot) + padma (lotus) + makaranda (nectar, honey-juice). The signature Gauḍīya phrase. Bhagavān's feet are the lotus; the bee is the bhakta; the makaranda is rasa. Cf. SB 10.31.9 in the gopīs' songs of separation.
    • munīnām — for sages
      Genitive plural of muni. Even sages — those silently pondering — find His path 'not apparent.' She is laying the ground: if even munis cannot read Him, my fainting (v. 24) is no defect of insight, only the natural inscrutability of His līlā.
    • alaukikam — supramundane
      A (not) + laukika (worldly). His īhita (activities) are a-laukika. The very word He used in v. 13 (aloka-patham, 'path not acceptable to worldly') she now turns to praise: a-laukika is precisely what makes Him Bhagavān.
    • anu — following
      Prefix indicating sequential conformity. 'Those who follow You' — anu-yāyin, the devotees. Their activities too are alaukika; the bhakta inherits the unworldliness of the Beloved. Gauḍīya doctrine in a single particle.
    Your movements, inscrutable even for sages who relish the honey of Your lotus feet, are certainly incomprehensible for human beings who behave like animals. And just as Your activities are transcendental, O all-powerful Lord, so too are those of Your followers.
    Purport

    Here Queen Rukmiṇī replies to Lord Kṛṣṇa’s statement in text 13: aspaṣṭa-vartmanāṁ puṁsām aloka-patham īyuṣām āsthitāḥ padavīṁ su-bhru prāyaḥ sīdanti yoṣitaḥ “O fine-browed lady, women are usually destined to suffer when they stay with men whose behavior is uncertain and who pursue a path not approved by society.” In the present verse Rukmiṇī is taking the term aloka-patham to mean “unworldly path.” Those who are entangled in worldly behavior are trying to enjoy this world more or less like animals. Even if such people are “culturally advanced,” they should simply be considered sophisticated or polished animals. Śrīmatī Rukmiṇī-devī points out that because the Lord’s activities are always transcendental, they are aspaṣṭa, or “unclear,” to ordinary people, and even the sages trying to know the Lord cannot perfectly understand these activities.

    — A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupāda
    Gauḍīya Ācāryas
    Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura Gauḍīya
    Translation
    Your movements, inscrutable even for sages who relish the honey of Your lotus feet, are certainly incomprehensible for human beings who behave like animals. And just as Your activities are transcendental, O all-powerful Lord, so too are those of Your followers.
    Commentary

    In this verse she replies to Krsna ’s statement that his path is unclear. "Yes it is true, your path is unclear even to the munis. Certainly it is incomprehensible to the animalistic men. It is true that you do not follow the customary path. As your activities are uncommon, so also those who follow you have uncommon activities.

    Jīva Gosvāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Nanu is an exclamation in prema or it means certainly. Your favorite activities cannot be understood by jṣānis who relish the sweetness of your feet by the influence of association with your devotees. Since your activities are covered by other actions to conciliate the public, they cannot be understood at all by unintelligent men. However those with proper intelligence can understand. This is the answer to Kṛṣṇa’s remark that his path is unclear. You also do not perform the actions of ordinary people. Your activities are beyond the material realm, though they appear ordinary (iva), because your glories are constant (bhūman).

    Śrīdhara Svāmī Gauḍīya
    Commentary

    Jṣānīs (munīnām) also by association with devotees relish the honey or bhakti-rasa from your lotus feet. The devotees of course relish this and more so your close associates. Nanu is an exclamation in prema or means certainly. Your conduct is independent (asphutam) of them, just as persons intoxicated with liquor fail to act according to normal rules, not thinking clearly. Your conduct cannot be understood by persons who are like animals. It can be understood by persons having proper intelligence, since they are not qualified for regular duties. tāvat karmāṇi kurvīta na nirvidyeta yāvatā mat-kathā-śravaṇādau vā śraddhā yāvan na jāyate As long as one does not become detached from daily and periodic duties or has not awakened his faith in hearing topics about me, one must perform one’s prescribed duties of varṇāśrama. SB 11.20.9 One may speculate about their intentions. Though it is said that one should know karma and vikarma (BG 4.17), some devotee may even engage in vikarma. This verse answers the statement in verse 13 aloka-patham īyuṣām: women suffer from men whose behavior is uncertain and who pursue a path not approved by society. Alaukikam īhitam mean conduct which is beyond the material world. But this is only apparent (iva) since you generally act properly, so that people can follow such conduct. Or alaukikam can means “not in excess of what is commonly said or done.” This is cause you are have unlimited greatness (bhūman). Bound the rules of the world you would be limited. You are qualified for activities beyond this world. Or your conduct is independent because your actions are certainly (iva) beyond this world. Iva here means eva. Even the devotees’ actions are beyond the world. Thus the answer has been given to aloka-patham īyūṣam in verse 13. Or aspaṣṭha-vartmanām is answered with alaukikam īhitam. This is certain (nanu).

    Personal Guidance
    Your movements are incomprehensible even for sages relishing the honey of Your lotus feet — let alone for human beings behaving like animals. Rukmiṇī uses the Lord's transcendence to argue she chose Him precisely as the right choice.
    Reflection Questions
    • Where do you mistake your inability to comprehend Him for His unworthiness?
    • How does incomprehensibility actually qualify Him as Supreme?
    Analogy

    Bees that have tasted the honey of a particular flower can describe its taste only by humming, not by speaking. So sages who have tasted His pada-padma-makaranda speak inscrutably even to other humans — and humans who behave like animals cannot read them. The verse marks two tiers above the worldly.
